terms.meaning: A toolkit that helps build mobile apps with one shared code base.
A reusable library of code that the app downloads and uses.
A group of related projects in one repository that share packages.
A version rule that allows small updates within the same minor version.
Checking code for style and common mistakes.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Mobile app package list
sections.what: Lists the app name, the start, test, lint, and check commands, and all the mobile libraries and development tools.
sections.why: This file is the single list the package manager uses to install the mobile app.
sections.watch_out: Changing one Expo library version without the others can break the app, so keep them compatible.

summary: Lists the scripts and libraries for the mobile app built with Expo, including camera, notifications, secure storage, and state tools.
purpose: Tells the package manager which libraries the mobile app needs and gives short commands to run, test, and check it.
why: Expo versions are pinned to tilde ranges so updates stay within a compatible set, which is a standard way to keep Expo apps working together.
how: Lists the app name and version, the scripts for starting, testing, linting, type checking, and cleaning, then the runtime libraries and the development tools.
inputs: The installed package versions and the scripts run by a developer.
outputs: A working set of installed packages and runnable scripts.
risks: The build script only prints a message and does not build the app, so production builds must use the separate build service. Some versions are pinned to tilde ranges that can still change within a minor version. Axios and the query library are listed here, which may duplicate the web setup.
debug: If install fails, check that the shared workspace packages exist. If the app fails to start, check the Expo version matches the installed React Native version. If tests fail to run, check the test script and jest setup.
